page: Amazon Web Services r6a.4xlarge is a memory-optimized instance built on the Nitro hypervisor architecture. It features an AMD EPYC 7R13 processor clocked at 3.6 GHz, providing 16 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 8 physical cores with 2 threads per core. Memory capacity is substantial, provisioned with 128.0 GB of DDR4 RAM operating at 3 GHz, maintaining an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio (8.0 GB per vCPU). The instance does not include bundled local storage or integrated hardware accelerators, relying entirely on network-attached storage architectures, supported by a baseline network bandwidth of 6 Gbps.

Benchmark evaluations reveal a balance centered around typical memory-heavy system loads. The single-core compute performance measures strong in stress-ng at 2993.09 points, while multi-core compute sits squarely in the mid-range with a Geekbench multi-core score of 9665.0 and a PassMark CPU score of 23587.87. Memory throughput shows high cache velocity at 1138.78 GB/sec for small 16 KB read blocks, but drops noticeably on larger 256 MB uncached workloads to 39.03 GB/sec read and 22.1 GB/sec write. In-memory operations achieve 17.73 million Redis SET operations per second, with static web throughput recorded at 16.41 GB/sec.

Hardware tradeoffs are primarily defined by the absence of local NVMe storage, requiring dependency on remote network volumes, and the lack of advanced vector extensions like AVX-512. Due to the absence of dedicated accelerators and limited uncached throughput, larger machine learning workloads demonstrate reduced throughput, delivering 8.14 tokens/sec on 7B LLM text generation and 3.61 tokens/sec on 70B prompt processing. However, the high memory density provides efficient resource pooling for memory-bound applications without paying the premium associated with GPU or high-frequency compute clusters.

The AWS r6a.4xlarge is tailored for in-memory caching solutions, mid-tier relational database backends, large enterprise resource planning (ERP) systems, and memory-intensive real-time analytics pipelines.
description: Amazon Web Services r6a.4xlarge is a memory-optimized Nitro instance powered by a 16-vCPU AMD EPYC 7R13 processor running at 3.6 GHz across 8 physical cores. Configured with 128.0 GB of DDR4 memory, it delivers an 8:1 memory-to-core ratio suited for large in-memory footprints. The instance provides 6 Gbps baseline network throughput, contains zero GPUs, and includes no local storage. Benchmark figures place general compute and cache-line memory access in average-to-strong tiers, posting 17.73 million Redis SET operations per second and a single-core stress-ng rating of 2993.09, though uncached large-block memory streaming remains comparatively constrained. The absence of local NVMe and vector extensions limits high-throughput LLM execution and storage-intensive write bursts. Consequently, r6a.4xlarge is primarily suited for enterprise database clusters, distributed in-memory caches, and memory-intensive data processing pipelines.
